title: Building a dice-combat roguelite in Godot with GPT, Claude Code, and AI-generated art, give me your thoughts :)
author: mtgkev
selftext:
I’m the solo developer of Overload Protocol, a sci-fi dice-combat roguelite I've been working on for a few months built in Godot with AI assistance across development and art.

You choose three units, roll d20s to determine their abilities, then plan your targets and firing order with enemy rolls already visible. Between battles, you collect gear and relics and evolve your squad. Slay the Spire, Into the Breach, and Slice & Dice were big inspirations.

My tools have been GPT Astra, Terra alongside Claude Code - mostly Opus, with some Fable. The initial art direction was inspired by Retro Diffusion, and I used ChatGPT image generation to create the other artwork in a similar style. I also used Claude Design for UI inspiration.

I’m sharing an actual playable build rather than just screenshots, and I’d love feedback on how it holds together as a game. Does it feel like complete AI slop? Does the tutorial explain the basics alright? Is the gameplay loop interesting enough?

Play here: [https://kevmtg.itch.io/overload-protocol](https://kevmtg.itch.io/overload-protocol)

It runs in a browser on mobile or desktop, with a portrait layout designed for phones. The initial download is around 100 MB, so the first load can take a little while. Balance, tutorial pacing, and audio are still being refined.

Happy to answer questions about the tools and process too.
